resultados.refuerzo: Llevar is an infinitive, and after que the verb must be conjugated.
Descanses is the subjunctive tú form, used in wishes that begin with que.
Descansas is indicative; a wish with que needs the subjunctive, descanses.
Parecerse takes a before the person you resemble: se parece a su padre.
De marks origin or possession, not the person you resemble; parecerse takes a.
Con means with; parecerse does not use it, it takes a.
Both is wrong: the question asks for one sister only.
Portarse bien means to behave well; the verb agrees with niños, so portan.
Romper con means to break up with someone, so con is the right preposition.
Pedir cita is the set phrase for asking for an appointment at a clinic.
Oculista comes from ojo: the doctor who looks after your eyes.
Crudo means raw, not cooked; frito and hervido both describe cooked food.
A lot of fat is a distractor; the question asks about protein and fibre.
Salt is a distractor; the question asks what the pulses have, not salt.
Asar means to roast, the right verb for cooking a chicken in the oven.
Muy hecha means well done, the way to order a steak cooked all the way through.
Venir is an infinitive; after que it must be conjugated, here venga.
Al casero is a plus el; the landlord is the person you pay rent to.
Arreglar is an infinitive; para que needs a conjugated verb, here arregle.
De shows what material something is made of: una camisa de algodón.
En marks a place, not the material; for what something is made of, use de.
Con means with; to say what something is made of, use de.
Devolver is an infinitive; prefiere que needs a subjunctive, here devolvamos.
Lonchas means thin slices, the right word for ham cut thin.
Latas means tins or cans, not slices of ham.
Disfrazarse de means to dress up as, and it always takes de.
La luna de miel is the honeymoon, the trip a couple takes after the wedding.
Cenar is an infinitive; es costumbre que takes the subjunctive, cenen.
Traer is an infinitive; hace falta que needs a subjunctive, traigas.
Bastar con means to be enough with something, so con is correct.
Devolver is an infinitive; ruego que needs a subjunctive, devuelvan.
Late arrival is a distractor; the question asks for the reason the text gives.
Not paying is a distractor; check which reason the text actually gives.
Peatones means pedestrians, the people who walk across the crossing.
Empatar means to draw, the result when neither team wins.
Perdieron means they lost, but neither team won, so it does not fit.
Ganaron means they won, which contradicts the sentence: neither team won.
El árbitro is the referee, who rules on whether a goal counts.
El entrenador is the coach; he trains the team but does not rule on goals.
El aficionado is the fan; he watches the match but has no say in the call.
